quiz.q: What is the product of acetylation of salicylic acid with acetic anhydride?
quiz.explain: The phenolic OH of salicylic acid is acetylated to form aspirin.
quiz.mistake: Confuses acetylation with methylation

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Tertiary alcohols undergo dehydration more readily than primary alcohols. Reason (R): Dehydration proceeds through a carbocation intermediate, and tertiary carbocations are the most stable.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
quiz.explain: The more stable the carbocation, the faster the slow step, so 3° alcohols dehydrate under milder conditions.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect carbocation stability with rate

teach.ask: Gappu has three unknown alcohols: 'How can I tell which is primary, secondary or tertiary in a test tube?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Lucas reagent: tertiary turns cloudy at once, secondary in a few minutes, primary stays clear at room temperature!
teach.nudge: Which test, and how fast does each class of alcohol turn cloudy?

topics.title: Oxidation of alcohols and distinguishing tests

learn.hook: Breathalysers used by traffic police once relied on orange dichromate turning green as it oxidised ethanol. Oxidation is also how we tell 1°, 2° and 3° alcohols apart.
points: Primary alcohols are oxidised to aldehydes and then to carboxylic acids. Strong oxidants (acidified KMnO₄, K₂Cr₂O₇) give acids; to stop at the aldehyde use CrO₃ in anhydrous medium or PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate, a complex of CrO₃ with pyridine and HCl).
Secondary alcohols are oxidised to ketones (e.g. by CrO₃). Tertiary alcohols resist oxidation; under strong conditions (KMnO₄, heat) they break into a mixture of acids with fewer carbon atoms.
Dehydrogenation over hot copper at 573 K: 1° alcohol → aldehyde; 2° alcohol → ketone; 3° alcohol → alkene (dehydration), e.g. 2-methylpropan-2-ol → 2-methylpropene.

Distinguishing tests: neutral FeCl₃ gives a violet colour with phenol (alcohols do not); bromine water gives a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol with phenol; Lucas test classifies alcohols; alcohols with CH₃CH(OH)– (e.g. ethanol, propan-2-ol) give a yellow iodoform precipitate with I₂/NaOH.

example.q: How would you distinguish between ethanol and phenol?
steps: Add neutral FeCl₃ solution to each
Ethanol gives no such colour (also, ethanol gives the iodoform test, phenol does not)
example.answer: Phenol gives a violet colour with neutral FeCl₃; ethanol does not

learn.reallife: Modern breath-analysers mostly use fuel-cell sensors, but the classic dichromate test is still a favourite Class 12 demonstration of alcohol oxidation.

games.title: Which test is positive?
items: Reacts with aqueous NaOH to form a salt
Gives an aldehyde when passed over hot copper at 573 K

quiz.q: Which reagent oxidises a primary alcohol only up to the aldehyde stage?
quiz.explain: PCC is a mild oxidant that stops at the aldehyde.
quiz.mistake: Picks a strong oxidant that goes on to the acid

quiz.q: What is formed when propan-2-ol is oxidised with CrO₃?
quiz.explain: Secondary alcohols are oxidised to ketones.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 2° alcohols give aldehydes

quiz.q: What happens when 2-methylpropan-2-ol vapour is passed over hot copper at 573 K?
options: It is oxidised to an aldehyde
It is oxidised to a ketone
quiz.explain: Tertiary alcohols have no H on the carbinol carbon, so they lose water instead of being dehydrogenated.
quiz.mistake: Assumes all alcohols give carbonyl compounds

quiz.q: Which test distinguishes phenol from ethanol?
options: Lucas reagent reacts only with phenol
Both give a violet colour with FeCl₃
Neutral FeCl₃ gives a violet colour with phenol
Sodium metal reacts only with ethanol
quiz.explain: Phenols form a violet complex with Fe³⁺; alcohols do not.
quiz.mistake: Thinks sodium distinguishes them (both react)

quiz.q: Which alcohol gives a positive iodoform test?
quiz.explain: Propan-2-ol has the CH₃CH(OH)– group, which is oxidised to CH₃CO– and then gives CHI₃.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every alcohol gives iodoform

quiz.q: What is the final product when ethanol is oxidised with excess acidified K₂Cr₂O₇?
quiz.explain: Ethanol → ethanal → ethanoic acid with a strong oxidant in excess.
quiz.mistake: Stops at the aldehyde

quiz.q: How do tertiary alcohols behave towards mild oxidising agents?
options: They give carboxylic acids with the same number of carbons
quiz.explain: There is no H on the carbon bearing OH, so mild oxidation does not occur.
quiz.mistake: Assumes all alcohols oxidise easily

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Phenol gives a white precipitate with bromine water but ethanol does not. Reason (R): The –OH group strongly activates the benzene ring towards electrophilic substitution.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
quiz.explain: The activated ring of phenol reacts at once with bromine water to give 2,4,6-tribromophenol; ethanol has no ring.
quiz.mistake: Does not link ring activation to the test

teach.ask: Gappu has two bottles: 'How can I tell propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol apart by oxidation?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Mild oxidation turns propan-1-ol into an aldehyde and propan-2-ol into a ketone. Different products, different alcohols!
teach.nudge: What does each one give on mild oxidation?

topics.title: Reactions of phenol: electrophilic substitution and named reactions

learn.hook: Aspirin starts from salicylic acid, which comes from phenol by Kolbe's reaction. Phenol's super-activated ring makes such chemistry easy.
points: The –OH group strongly activates the ring and directs electrophiles to ortho and para positions.

Nitration: dilute HNO₃ at 298 K gives o- and p-nitrophenol, separated by steam distillation (o-nitrophenol is steam volatile because of intramolecular H-bonding; p-nitrophenol has intermolecular H-bonding). Concentrated HNO₃ gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid), better made via phenol-2,4-disulphonic acid.
Halogenation: Br₂ in CS₂ or CHCl₃ at low temperature gives mono-bromophenols (mainly para) without a Lewis acid; bromine water gives a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

Kolbe's reaction: sodium phenoxide + CO₂, then acid → 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid). Reimer–Tiemann reaction: phenol + CHCl₃ + aqueous NaOH, then acid → 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde).
Phenol heated with zinc dust gives benzene. Oxidation with chromic acid gives benzoquinone (a conjugated diketone); on standing in air, phenols slowly form dark coloured mixtures containing quinones.

example.q: How are o- and p-nitrophenol separated after nitration of phenol?
steps: o-Nitrophenol has an intramolecular H-bond (between –OH and –NO₂ on adjacent carbons)
So it does not associate and is steam volatile
p-Nitrophenol forms intermolecular H-bonds and is not steam volatile
example.answer: By steam distillation: o-nitrophenol distils over

learn.reallife: Methyl salicylate (from salicylic acid) gives many Indian pain-relief balms their wintergreen smell; salicylic acid itself is made from phenol by Kolbe's reaction.

games.title: Phenol reactions
items: Bromination of phenol requires a Lewis acid catalyst.
The ring is so activated that no Lewis acid is needed.
Kolbe's reaction gives salicylic acid; Reimer–Tiemann gives salicylaldehyde.
Phenol is converted into benzene by heating with zinc dust.
Zinc removes the oxygen as ZnO.
Bromine in CS₂ at low temperature gives mainly p-bromophenol.
Mild conditions give mono-substitution, mostly para.

quiz.q: What is the product of Kolbe's reaction?
quiz.explain: Sodium phenoxide reacts with CO₂ (a weak electrophile), and acidification gives salicylic acid.
quiz.mistake: Confuses Kolbe with Reimer–Tiemann

quiz.q: What is the product of the Reimer–Tiemann reaction of phenol?
quiz.explain: CHCl₃ and NaOH introduce a –CHO group at the ortho position after hydrolysis.
quiz.mistake: Gives the Kolbe product

quiz.q: What is formed when phenol is treated with bromine water?
quiz.explain: In water, bromine reacts at all three activated positions (two ortho, one para).
quiz.mistake: Assumes only monobromination

quiz.q: Why is o-nitrophenol more volatile than p-nitrophenol?
options: o-Nitrophenol forms intramolecular hydrogen bonds, while p-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds
p-Nitrophenol has a lower molar mass
quiz.explain: Intramolecular H-bonding prevents association of o-nitrophenol molecules.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the isomers have different masses

quiz.q: What is obtained when phenol is heated with zinc dust?
quiz.explain: Zinc dust reduces phenol to benzene, forming ZnO.
quiz.mistake: Thinks zinc oxidises phenol

quiz.q: What is formed when phenol is oxidised with chromic acid?
quiz.explain: Phenol is oxidised to the conjugated diketone benzoquinone.
quiz.mistake: Assumes oxidation gives an acid

quiz.q: Why does phenol undergo bromination even without a Lewis acid?
options: The –OH group strongly activates the ring, polarising the bromine molecule
Phenol contains a built-in Lewis acid
quiz.explain: The ring is so electron-rich that Br₂ is polarised enough without FeBr₃.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a catalyst is always required

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Sodium phenoxide reacts with CO₂, a weak electrophile, while phenol itself does not under the same conditions. Reason (R): Phenoxide ion is more reactive than phenol towards electrophilic substitution.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
quiz.explain: The negative charge on O makes the ring of phenoxide even more electron-rich, so it can react with weak electrophiles like CO₂.
quiz.mistake: Does not see why phenoxide is used in Kolbe's reaction

teach.ask: Gappu mixes up names: 'What's the difference between Kolbe's and Reimer–Tiemann reactions?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Kolbe: phenoxide + CO₂ gives salicylic acid; Reimer–Tiemann: CHCl₃ + NaOH gives salicylaldehyde. Both go ortho!
teach.nudge: Which reagent does each use, and what product does each give?

topics.title: Commercially important alcohols: methanol and ethanol

learn.hook: India's E20 petrol blends ethanol from sugarcane molasses into fuel. Its cousin methanol, however, is a deadly poison if swallowed.
points: Methanol (wood spirit) was once made by destructive distillation of wood. Today it is made by catalytic hydrogenation of carbon monoxide: CO + 2H₂ →(ZnO–Cr₂O₃, 200–300 atm, 573–673 K) CH₃OH.
Methanol is highly poisonous: drinking even small amounts can cause blindness, and larger amounts cause death. It is used as a solvent for paints and varnishes and to make formaldehyde.

Ethanol is made by fermentation of sugars (from molasses, sugarcane or fruits like grapes) using yeast enzymes: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O →(invertase) C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + C₆H₁₂O₆ (fructose); C₆H₁₂O₆ →(zymase) 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. Fermentation is anaerobic; if air enters, ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid, making the product sour.
Commercial ethanol is made unfit for drinking by adding copper sulphate (to colour it) and pyridine (a foul-smelling liquid): this is denatured alcohol.
Uses of ethanol: solvent in the paint industry, in making many carbon compounds, and as a fuel blended with petrol.

example.q: Write the two enzyme-catalysed steps in making ethanol from sucrose.
steps: Both enzymes come from yeast; conditions are anaerobic
example.answer: Invertase hydrolyses sucrose; zymase ferments the hexoses to ethanol and CO₂

learn.reallife: Sugar mills in Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh run distilleries that turn molasses into fuel ethanol for blending with petrol under India's ethanol-blending programme.

games.title: From molasses to ethanol
items: Dilute molasses (rich in sucrose) with water
Add yeast and keep away from air
Invertase hydrolyses sucrose to glucose and fructose
Zymase converts the hexoses into ethanol and CO₂
Distil the fermented liquid to concentrate ethanol

games.title: Methanol or ethanol?
items: Can cause blindness even in small amounts
Blended with petrol in E20 fuel

quiz.q: Which catalyst is used for the industrial manufacture of methanol from CO and H₂?
quiz.explain: CO + 2H₂ → CH₃OH over ZnO–Cr₂O₃ at 200–300 atm and 573–673 K.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with other industrial catalysts

quiz.q: Which enzyme converts glucose into ethanol during fermentation?
quiz.explain: Zymase from yeast ferments glucose (and fructose) to ethanol and CO₂.
quiz.mistake: Gives the enzyme that hydrolyses sucrose

quiz.q: Why does a fermented drink turn sour when air gets in?
options: Ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid
CO₂ dissolves to form carbonic acid only
quiz.explain: Oxygen allows bacteria to oxidise ethanol to acetic acid.
quiz.mistake: Credits the sourness to CO₂

quiz.q: What is denatured alcohol?
options: A mixture of ethanol and water at 95%
Ethanol made unfit for drinking by adding copper sulphate and pyridine
quiz.explain: Additives give colour and a foul smell to discourage drinking.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with rectified spirit

quiz.q: What is the danger of drinking methanol?
options: It can cause blindness and, in larger amounts, death
It is harmless in small amounts
quiz.explain: Methanol is highly poisonous even in small quantities.
quiz.mistake: Thinks methanol is as safe as ethanol in small amounts

quiz.q: How many moles of CO₂ are produced when 1 mol of glucose is fermented completely to ethanol?
quiz.explain: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂.
quiz.mistake: Uses the respiration equation (6 CO₂)

quiz.q: What is the role of invertase in making ethanol from cane sugar?
options: It hydrolyses sucrose into glucose and fructose
quiz.explain: Invertase breaks sucrose into the two hexoses that zymase can ferment.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the roles of the two enzymes

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Fermentation of sugar to ethanol is carried out in the absence of air. Reason (R): In the presence of air, ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.explain: Keeping air out prevents the ethanol formed from being oxidised to acetic acid.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect air with oxidation of ethanol

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How is ethanol made from molasses, and why is methanol so dangerous?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Yeast enzymes ferment sugar to ethanol without air, but methanol is poisonous and can cause blindness. Safety first!
teach.nudge: How does yeast make ethanol, and what is the danger of methanol?

topics.title: Ethers: preparation and physical properties

learn.hook: Diethyl ether was first publicly demonstrated as a surgical anaesthetic in 1846. Making ethers looks easy, but choosing the wrong alkyl halide gives you an alkene instead.
points: Dehydration of alcohols: 2C₂H₅OH →(conc. H₂SO₄, 413 K) C₂H₅OC₂H₅ + H₂O. It proceeds by SN2 attack of an alcohol molecule on a protonated alcohol. It works for primary alcohols; secondary and tertiary alcohols give alkenes. Temperature matters: at 443 K ethanol gives ethene.
Williamson synthesis: R–X + R′–O⁻Na⁺ → R–O–R′ + NaX. It makes both symmetrical and unsymmetrical ethers, and works by SN2.

The alkyl halide must be primary. With a tertiary halide, the alkoxide acts as a base and elimination gives an alkene: (CH₃)₃CBr + CH₃ONa → (CH₃)₂C=CH₂. Correct route: (CH₃)₃C–ONa + CH₃Br → (CH₃)₃C–O–CH₃.
Alkyl aryl ethers are made from phenoxide and an alkyl halide: C₆H₅O⁻Na⁺ + CH₃I → C₆H₅OCH₃ (anisole).

Ethers have a bent, weakly polar C–O–C group. Their boiling points are close to alkanes of similar mass (n-pentane 309.1 K, ethoxyethane 307.6 K) and far below alcohols (butan-1-ol 390 K), because ethers cannot H-bond with each other. Their water solubility is similar to alcohols of similar mass because the ether oxygen can H-bond with water.

example.q: Which pair of reagents should be used to make 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane by Williamson synthesis?
steps: Option 2: (CH₃)₃CONa + CH₃Br → SN2 on a methyl halide works well

learn.reallife: Diethyl ether is a common solvent in college labs across India; it is kept away from flames because it is extremely flammable and its vapour is heavier than air.

games.title: Boiling points of compounds of similar mass
Ether preparation
items: Williamson synthesis works best with primary alkyl halides.
Tertiary alkyl halides give ethers in high yield in Williamson synthesis.
Ethanol with conc. H₂SO₄ at 413 K gives ethoxyethane.
At this temperature intermolecular dehydration occurs.
Ethers form strong hydrogen bonds with each other.
They have no O–H, so they cannot H-bond among themselves.
Ethers dissolve in water about as well as alcohols of similar mass.
The ether oxygen can accept H-bonds from water.
Anisole can be made from sodium phenoxide and methyl iodide.

quiz.q: What is the product when ethanol is heated with conc. H₂SO₄ at 413 K?
quiz.explain: At 413 K, two ethanol molecules lose water to form diethyl ether.
quiz.mistake: Uses the 443 K product

quiz.q: Which reagents give the best yield of 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane?
quiz.explain: The alkyl halide must be primary (here methyl) for SN2; a tertiary halide would eliminate.
quiz.mistake: Uses a tertiary halide

quiz.q: What happens when (CH₃)₃CBr is treated with sodium methoxide?
options: Methanol and tert-butyl bromide exchange groups
quiz.explain: The strongly basic methoxide removes a β-hydrogen from the crowded tertiary halide.
quiz.mistake: Expects substitution with a tertiary halide

quiz.q: Why is the dehydration method unsuitable for making ethers from secondary and tertiary alcohols?
options: These alcohols readily dehydrate to alkenes instead
They do not react with acids
quiz.explain: Elimination competes strongly with substitution for 2° and 3° alcohols.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all alcohols behave like ethanol

quiz.q: Why do ethers have much lower boiling points than isomeric alcohols?
options: Ethers have stronger van der Waals forces
Ether molecules cannot form hydrogen bonds with each other
quiz.explain: Without O–H, ethers lack intermolecular H-bonding.
quiz.mistake: Thinks isomers have different masses

quiz.q: Why is ethoxyethane about as soluble in water as butan-1-ol?
options: The ether oxygen can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules
quiz.explain: Water's hydrogen atoms bond to the lone pairs on the ether oxygen.
quiz.mistake: Thinks ethers cannot interact with water at all

quiz.q: Which reaction is used to prepare anisole?
options: Chlorobenzene with sodium methoxide at room temperature
Phenol with methanol and conc. H₂SO₄
quiz.explain: Phenoxide is a good nucleophile and CH₃I a good SN2 substrate; aryl halides do not undergo SN2.
quiz.mistake: Uses an aryl halide as the substrate

quiz.q: Assertion (A): In Williamson synthesis, primary alkyl halides are preferred. Reason (R): The reaction proceeds by an SN2 mechanism, and with tertiary halides the alkoxide acts as a base causing elimination.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.explain: SN2 needs an unhindered carbon, and tertiary halides prefer elimination with strong bases.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the mechanism to the choice of halide

teach.ask: Gappu wants an ether: 'In Williamson synthesis, why must I use a primary alkyl halide?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Williamson is SN2, which needs an unhindered halide; a tertiary halide just eliminates to an alkene!
teach.nudge: What mechanism does Williamson synthesis follow, and what goes wrong with tertiary halides?

topics.title: Reactions of ethers

learn.hook: Ethers are famously unreactive, which makes them great solvents. Yet hot concentrated HI can split them apart, and anisole's ring is eager for electrophiles.
points: Ethers are cleaved by hydrogen halides: R–O–R + HX → R–X + R–OH; with excess HX the alcohol is also converted to R–X. Reactivity: HI > HBr > HCl, following the nucleophilicity of the halide ion.

For mixed dialkyl ethers with primary/methyl groups, the halide attacks the smaller group by SN2: CH₃–O–C₂H₅ + HI → CH₃I + C₂H₅OH. If one group is tertiary, the reaction goes by SN1 and the tertiary halide forms: (CH₃)₃C–O–CH₃ + HI → (CH₃)₃C–I + CH₃OH.

Alkyl aryl ethers are cleaved at the alkyl–oxygen bond: C₆H₅–O–CH₃ + HI → C₆H₅OH + CH₃I. The O–aryl bond has partial double bond character, and the sp² carbon cannot undergo SN1 or SN2, so phenol does not turn into an aryl halide.

The –OCH₃ group activates the ring and directs ortho/para. Anisole + Br₂ in ethanoic acid (no FeBr₃ needed) → mainly p-bromoanisole; Friedel–Crafts with CH₃Cl/AlCl₃ → 2- and 4-methoxytoluene; with CH₃COCl/AlCl₃ → 2- and 4-methoxyacetophenone; nitration (conc. HNO₃ + H₂SO₄) → 2- and 4-nitroanisole (para major).

example.q: Predict the products of heating anisole with HI.
steps: I⁻ attacks the methyl carbon (SN2); the phenyl–O bond is stronger and cannot be attacked

learn.reallife: Anethole, a methoxybenzene derivative, gives saunf (fennel) and aniseed their sweet flavour; the methoxy group's ortho/para directing power helps chemists build such molecules.

games.title: Reactivity of HX towards cleavage of ethers

quiz.q: What are the products when anisole is heated with HI?
quiz.explain: The O–CH₃ bond is cleaved; the O–phenyl bond has partial double bond character and is not attacked.
quiz.mistake: Breaks the aryl–oxygen bond

quiz.q: What are the products when methoxyethane reacts with one equivalent of HI?
quiz.explain: By SN2, I⁻ attacks the less hindered methyl group.
quiz.mistake: Puts iodine on the larger group

quiz.q: What are the products of the reaction of 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane with HI?
quiz.explain: With a tertiary group, the reaction goes via the stable tertiary carbocation (SN1), so the tertiary iodide forms.
quiz.mistake: Applies the SN2 rule to a tertiary ether

quiz.q: Arrange HCl, HBr and HI in increasing order of reactivity towards ether cleavage.
quiz.explain: Iodide is the best nucleophile and HI the strongest acid of the three.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the order

quiz.q: Why does phenol formed from anisole not react further with HI to form iodobenzene?
options: The sp² carbon–oxygen bond of phenol has partial double bond character and does not undergo SN1/SN2
quiz.explain: The aryl C–O bond resists nucleophilic substitution.
quiz.mistake: Assumes phenol behaves like an alcohol

quiz.q: What is the major product of nitration of anisole?
quiz.explain: –OCH₃ is ortho/para directing; the para product is major.
quiz.mistake: Thinks –OCH₃ is meta directing

quiz.q: Why does bromination of anisole not require FeBr₃?
options: The –OCH₃ group activates the ring strongly
quiz.explain: The electron-donating methoxy group makes the ring reactive enough for Br₂ in ethanoic acid.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a Lewis acid is always needed

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Ethers are commonly used as solvents for reactions. Reason (R): Ethers are relatively unreactive under ordinary conditions.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
quiz.explain: Their low reactivity means they do not interfere with most reagents, such as Grignard reagents.
quiz.mistake: Does not link inertness to usefulness as a solvent

teach.ask: Gappu splits anisole with HI: 'Why do I get phenol and methyl iodide, not iodobenzene and methanol?'
teach.praise: Chirp! The aryl–O bond has partial double bond character, so HI breaks the weaker CH₃–O bond: phenol + CH₃I!
teach.nudge: Which C–O bond breaks, and why is the other one too strong?

topics.title: Nomenclature and structure of the carbonyl group

learn.hook: The vanilla in kulfi, the cinnamon in garam masala and the sharp smell of camphor (kapur) all come from aldehydes and ketones. They share one star: the C=O group.
points: Aldehydes have –CHO (carbonyl bonded to at least one H); ketones have C=O bonded to two carbon groups.

IUPAC: aldehydes end in -al, ketones in -one. HCHO methanal (formaldehyde), CH₃CHO ethanal (acetaldehyde), (CH₃)₂CHCHO 2-methylpropanal, CH₃CH=CHCHO but-2-enal, C₆H₅CHO benzenecarbaldehyde (benzaldehyde).
Ketones: CH₃COCH₃ propanone (acetone), CH₃COCH₂CH₃ butan-2-one (ethyl methyl ketone), C₆H₅COCH₃ 1-phenylethan-1-one (acetophenone), C₆H₅COC₆H₅ diphenylmethanone (benzophenone).
The carbonyl carbon is sp² hybridised and forms three σ bonds in one plane at about 120°; its unhybridised p orbital overlaps with oxygen's p orbital to form a π bond.
Oxygen is more electronegative, so the C=O bond is polar: the carbon is electrophilic (Lewis acid site) and the oxygen nucleophilic (Lewis base site). This is shown by the resonance C=O ↔ C⁺–O⁻.

example.q: Give the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂COCH₃.
steps: Number from the end nearer C=O: C=O at C-2, CH₃ at C-4

learn.reallife: Vanillin (an aldehyde) is the flavour in vanilla ice cream, and cinnamaldehyde gives dalchini (cinnamon) its aroma in Indian cooking.

games.title: Carbonyl structure
items: The carbonyl carbon is sp² hybridised.
It forms three σ bonds in a plane.
Bond angles around the carbonyl carbon are about 109.5°.
Oxygen pulls electron density away from it.
Oxygen is more electronegative, making it polar.
Resonance places a partial positive charge on carbon.

quiz.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃COCH₂CH₃?
quiz.explain: Four carbons with C=O at C-2 (numbered to give the lowest locant).
quiz.mistake: Numbers from the wrong end

quiz.q: What is the IUPAC name of C₆H₅COCH₃?
quiz.explain: Acetophenone is an ethanone with a phenyl group on the carbonyl carbon.
quiz.mistake: Treats the ketone as an aldehyde

quiz.q: What is the IUPAC name of (CH₃)₂CHCHO?
quiz.explain: The CHO carbon is C-1; a methyl group sits on C-2 of a propanal chain.
quiz.mistake: Uses -one for an aldehyde

quiz.q: What is the hybridisation of the carbonyl carbon?
quiz.explain: It forms three σ bonds and one π bond, in a trigonal planar arrangement.
quiz.mistake: Thinks C=O carbon is tetrahedral

quiz.q: Which statement about the carbonyl group is correct?
options: The carbon is nucleophilic and the oxygen is electrophilic
Both atoms carry no partial charge
The carbon is electrophilic and the oxygen is nucleophilic
quiz.explain: Polarisation of C=O leaves carbon partially positive and oxygen partially negative.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the polarity

quiz.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH=CHCHO?
quiz.explain: Number from the CHO carbon (C-1); the double bond starts at C-2.
quiz.mistake: Numbers from the CH₃ end

quiz.q: What is the approximate bond angle around the carbonyl carbon?
quiz.explain: sp² hybridisation gives a trigonal planar arrangement with angles near 120°.
quiz.mistake: Uses the tetrahedral angle

quiz.q: Assertion (A): The carbonyl carbon is attacked by nucleophiles. Reason (R): Due to the polarity of the C=O bond, the carbonyl carbon carries a partial positive charge.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.explain: The electron-poor carbon attracts electron-rich nucleophiles.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect polarity with reactivity

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What makes the carbon of a C=O group a target for nucleophiles?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Oxygen pulls electrons, leaving the sp² carbon partially positive — a perfect target for nucleophiles!
teach.nudge: Which atom is more electronegative, and what charge does that leave on carbon?

topics.title: Preparation of aldehydes and ketones: general methods and aldehyde-specific routes

learn.hook: The Rosenmund catalyst is deliberately 'poisoned' with barium sulphate so the reaction stops at the aldehyde. Sometimes chemists want a lazier catalyst!
points: Oxidation of alcohols: 1° alcohols → aldehydes and 2° alcohols → ketones (e.g. with PCC or K₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺ under controlled conditions). Dehydrogenation of alcohol vapours over heavy-metal catalysts (Ag or Cu) is used industrially.
Ozonolysis of alkenes followed by Zn dust and water gives aldehydes, ketones or both, depending on the alkene's substituents.
Hydration of alkynes: ethyne + H₂O (HgSO₄, dilute H₂SO₄) gives ethanal; other alkynes give ketones.
Rosenmund reduction: R–COCl + H₂ →(Pd on BaSO₄) R–CHO + HCl. BaSO₄ poisons the palladium so that the aldehyde is not reduced further to an alcohol.

From nitriles: Stephen reaction — R–CN + SnCl₂ + HCl → imine → hydrolysis → R–CHO. Nitriles and esters can also be reduced selectively to aldehydes by DIBAL-H [diisobutylaluminium hydride, AlH(i-Bu)₂] followed by hydrolysis; DIBAL-H leaves C=C bonds untouched.

example.q: How would you convert benzoyl chloride into benzaldehyde?
steps: BaSO₄ poisons Pd so the aldehyde is not reduced to benzyl alcohol
example.answer: Rosenmund reduction with H₂ over Pd–BaSO₄

learn.reallife: Indian bulk-drug makers use DIBAL-H in flavour and drug synthesis because it can stop at the aldehyde stage without disturbing other double bonds in the molecule.

quiz.q: What is the role of BaSO₄ in the Rosenmund reduction?
options: It poisons the Pd catalyst so the aldehyde is not reduced further to an alcohol
It increases the activity of Pd
quiz.explain: A partially deactivated catalyst stops the reduction at the aldehyde stage.
quiz.mistake: Thinks BaSO₄ speeds up the reaction

quiz.q: What is the product of the Stephen reaction of CH₃CN?
quiz.explain: SnCl₂/HCl reduces the nitrile to an imine, which hydrolyses to the aldehyde.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the nitrile is reduced to an amine

quiz.q: Which reagent converts CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₂CN into CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₂CHO without affecting the C=C bond?
quiz.explain: DIBAL-H selectively reduces nitriles (and esters) to aldehydes and leaves C=C alone.
quiz.mistake: Picks a reagent that also reduces C=C or the aldehyde

quiz.q: What is formed when ethyne is hydrated with HgSO₄ and dilute H₂SO₄?
quiz.explain: The enol formed first tautomerises to ethanal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks hydration of an alkyne gives an alcohol

quiz.q: What is obtained when propyne is hydrated in the presence of HgSO₄/H₂SO₄?
quiz.explain: Alkynes other than ethyne give ketones (Markovnikov hydration).
quiz.mistake: Assumes all alkynes give aldehydes

quiz.q: Which method converts a secondary alcohol into a ketone?
quiz.explain: Secondary alcohols are oxidised to ketones.
quiz.mistake: Uses an aldehyde-only method

quiz.q: What does ozonolysis of but-2-ene (followed by Zn/H₂O) give?
quiz.explain: The C=C splits in the middle, each half becoming CH₃CHO.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the carbon chain intact

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Esters can be converted into aldehydes using DIBAL-H. Reason (R): DIBAL-H is a strong reducing agent that always reduces esters completely to alcohols.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
quiz.explain: DIBAL-H at controlled conditions stops at the aldehyde; R is false.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every hydride reagent goes all the way to the alcohol

teach.ask: Gappu has an acid chloride: 'How can I turn it into an aldehyde without making an alcohol by accident?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Rosenmund reduction with H₂ over BaSO₄-poisoned Pd stops at the aldehyde. Clever!
teach.nudge: Which reduction, and why is the catalyst poisoned?

topics.title: Aromatic aldehydes from hydrocarbons; preparation of ketones

learn.hook: Bitter-almond aroma in sweets and badam-flavoured drinks often comes from benzaldehyde made from toluene. Chemists have several neat ways to stop the oxidation right at the aldehyde.
points: Etard reaction: toluene + chromyl chloride (CrO₂Cl₂) in CS₂ forms a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde.

Toluene + CrO₃ in acetic anhydride gives benzylidene diacetate, which is hydrolysed by aqueous acid to benzaldehyde. Side-chain chlorination of toluene (Cl₂, light) gives benzal chloride (C₆H₅CHCl₂), which on hydrolysis at 373 K gives benzaldehyde (a commercial method).
Gatterman–Koch reaction: benzene (or a derivative) + CO + HCl with anhydrous AlCl₃ or CuCl gives benzaldehyde.
Ketones from acyl chlorides: 2R–MgX + CdCl₂ → R₂Cd + 2Mg(X)Cl; then 2R′–COCl + R₂Cd → 2R′–CO–R + CdCl₂.
Ketones from nitriles: R–CN + R′MgX, then hydrolysis → R–CO–R′ (e.g. CH₃CH₂CN + C₆H₅MgBr → propiophenone, C₆H₅COCH₂CH₃). Friedel–Crafts acylation: benzene + R–COCl (anhydrous AlCl₃) → C₆H₅COR.

example.q: How can acetophenone be prepared from benzene?
example.answer: Benzene + ethanoyl chloride with anhydrous AlCl₃

learn.reallife: Benzaldehyde is used in Indian food and fragrance industries to give an almond-like flavour to sweets and syrups.

quiz.q: What is the Etard reaction?
options: Reduction of benzoyl chloride to benzaldehyde
Formylation of benzene with CO and HCl
Oxidation of toluene by chromyl chloride to benzaldehyde
Oxidation of toluene by KMnO₄ to benzoic acid
quiz.explain: CrO₂Cl₂ forms a complex with toluene which is hydrolysed to benzaldehyde.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with Rosenmund or Gatterman–Koch

quiz.q: Which reagents are used in the Gatterman–Koch reaction?
options: CO and HCl with anhydrous AlCl₃ or CuCl
quiz.explain: These reagents introduce a –CHO group into benzene.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the named reactions

quiz.q: What is the product of CH₃COCl with (CH₃)₂Cd?
quiz.explain: The methyl group from dimethylcadmium replaces Cl, giving CH₃COCH₃.
quiz.mistake: Counts carbons wrongly

quiz.q: What is obtained when ethanenitrile (CH₃CN) reacts with CH₃MgBr followed by hydrolysis?
quiz.explain: R–CN + R′MgX gives R–CO–R′ after hydrolysis: CH₃COCH₃.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the nitrile is reduced to an aldehyde

quiz.q: Why is dialkylcadmium preferred over a Grignard reagent for making ketones from acyl chlorides?
options: Grignard reagents do not react with acyl chlorides
Dialkylcadmium is less reactive and does not attack the ketone formed
Cadmium acts as a catalyst only
quiz.explain: A Grignard reagent would add further to the ketone to give a tertiary alcohol.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Grignard reagent is unreactive

quiz.q: What is formed when benzal chloride (C₆H₅CHCl₂) is hydrolysed at 373 K?
quiz.explain: Two Cl on the same carbon are replaced, and the gem-diol loses water to give –CHO.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the product is an alcohol

quiz.q: Which ketone is obtained when benzene reacts with ethanoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃?
quiz.explain: Friedel–Crafts acylation introduces CH₃CO– onto the ring.
quiz.mistake: Confuses acyl and aryl groups

quiz.q: Assertion (A): In the oxidation of toluene with CrO₃ in acetic anhydride, the aldehyde is protected as benzylidene diacetate. Reason (R): This prevents further oxidation of benzaldehyde to benzoic acid.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
quiz.explain: Trapping the aldehyde as a diacetate stops over-oxidation; acid hydrolysis then releases benzaldehyde.
quiz.mistake: Does not see why the intermediate is useful

teach.ask: Gappu has toluene: 'How do I oxidise toluene to benzaldehyde without going all the way to benzoic acid?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Use chromyl chloride (Etard) or CrO₃ in acetic anhydride, which traps the aldehyde before it becomes an acid!
teach.nudge: Which reagents trap the oxidation at the aldehyde stage?

topics.title: Physical properties, nucleophilic addition and relative reactivity

learn.hook: Acetone in nail-polish remover evaporates fast, yet boils higher than butane of similar mass. Its dipoles explain that — and its chemistry too.
points: Methanal is a gas; ethanal is a volatile liquid; other members are liquids or solids. Boiling points are higher than hydrocarbons and ethers of similar mass (dipole–dipole attraction) but lower than alcohols (no H-bonding between molecules). For M ≈ 58–60: n-butane 273 K < methoxyethane 281 K < propanal 322 K < acetone 329 K < propan-1-ol 370 K.

Lower members (methanal, ethanal, propanone) are miscible with water because they form H-bonds with water; solubility falls with longer chains. Lower aldehydes have sharp, pungent smells; larger ones are more fragrant.

Nucleophilic addition: the nucleophile attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon from a direction roughly perpendicular to the plane of the sp² orbitals; carbon changes from sp² to sp³, forming a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate, which takes up a proton to give the product.
Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones: sterically, ketones have two bulky groups hindering attack; electronically, two alkyl groups reduce the positive character of the carbonyl carbon more.
Benzaldehyde is less reactive than propanal because the benzene ring's resonance reduces the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon.

example.q: Arrange ethanal, propanone and methanal in increasing order of reactivity towards nucleophilic addition.
steps: Methanal: two H atoms, least hindered, most electrophilic
Propanone: two CH₃ groups — most hindered and least electrophilic

learn.reallife: Acetone is the main solvent in many nail-polish removers sold in India; its mixing with water comes from hydrogen bonding with water molecules.

games.title: Reactivity and mechanism
items: In nucleophilic addition, the carbonyl carbon changes from sp² to sp³.
Ketones are generally more reactive than aldehydes towards nucleophiles.
Aldehydes are more reactive (less hindrance, more electrophilic carbon).
Methanal is the most reactive carbonyl compound towards nucleophilic addition.
It has no alkyl groups to hinder or donate electrons.
Benzaldehyde is more reactive than propanal towards nucleophiles.
Ring resonance makes its carbonyl carbon less electrophilic.
It accepts hydrogen bonds from water.

quiz.q: Why do aldehydes and ketones have higher boiling points than hydrocarbons of similar mass?
options: Dipole–dipole attractions between polar C=O groups
quiz.explain: The polar carbonyl group gives strong dipole–dipole forces; there is no O–H for H-bonding among themselves.
quiz.mistake: Thinks carbonyl compounds H-bond with each other

quiz.q: Why do aldehydes and ketones have lower boiling points than alcohols of similar mass?
options: They cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with each other
They form stronger dipole interactions than alcohols
quiz.explain: Alcohols have O–H groups that H-bond between molecules.
quiz.mistake: Ignores hydrogen bonding in alcohols

quiz.q: Which is the most reactive towards nucleophilic addition?
quiz.explain: HCHO has no alkyl groups, so it is least hindered and most electrophilic.
quiz.mistake: Thinks larger molecules react faster

quiz.q: Why are ketones less reactive than aldehydes towards nucleophiles?
options: Two alkyl groups hinder attack and reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon
quiz.explain: Both steric and electronic (+I) effects of two alkyl groups lower reactivity.
quiz.mistake: Gives only one effect or the wrong one

quiz.q: Why is benzaldehyde less reactive than propanal towards nucleophilic addition?
options: Resonance with the benzene ring reduces the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon
quiz.explain: Delocalisation of electrons from the ring into C=O makes carbon less electrophilic.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the ring increases reactivity

quiz.q: What change in hybridisation of the carbonyl carbon occurs during nucleophilic addition?
quiz.explain: The trigonal planar carbon becomes tetrahedral in the alkoxide intermediate.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the change

quiz.q: Why are lower aldehydes and ketones such as propanone miscible with water?
options: They form hydrogen bonds with water molecules
quiz.explain: The carbonyl oxygen accepts H-bonds from water.
quiz.mistake: Thinks they cannot interact with water

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Propanal boils at a lower temperature than propan-1-ol. Reason (R): Propan-1-ol molecules are held by intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: H-bonding in the alcohol is stronger than dipole–dipole attraction in the aldehyde.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect H-bonding with boiling point

teach.ask: Gappu compares: 'Why does ethanal react with nucleophiles faster than acetone?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Acetone's two methyl groups crowd the carbon and reduce its positive charge, so ethanal reacts faster!
teach.nudge: Name the two effects of alkyl groups on the carbonyl carbon.

topics.title: Addition of HCN, NaHSO₃, Grignard reagents and alcohols

learn.hook: Chemists sometimes need to 'hide' a ketone while they work on another part of a molecule. Turning it into a ketal with ethylene glycol does the trick.
points: HCN adds to aldehydes and ketones to give cyanohydrins: >C=O + HCN → >C(OH)CN. The reaction is slow with pure HCN but is catalysed by a base, which generates the stronger nucleophile CN⁻. Cyanohydrins are useful synthetic intermediates.

Sodium hydrogensulphite (NaHSO₃) adds to give crystalline hydrogensulphite addition compounds. The equilibrium lies to the right for most aldehydes and to the left for most ketones (steric reasons). The adducts can be decomposed back by dilute acid or alkali, so this is used to separate and purify aldehydes.
Grignard reagents add to give alcohols after hydrolysis (methanal → 1°, other aldehydes → 2°, ketones → 3°).

Aldehydes + one equivalent of a monohydric alcohol in dry HCl give hemiacetals (alkoxy alcohols), and then acetals (gem-dialkoxy compounds). Ketones with ethylene glycol in dry HCl give cyclic ketals. Dry HCl protonates the carbonyl oxygen, making the carbon more electrophilic.
Acetals and ketals are hydrolysed back to the carbonyl compound by aqueous mineral acid, so they are used to protect carbonyl groups.

example.q: What is the product when ethanal reacts with HCN, and what type of compound is it?

learn.reallife: Protecting groups like ketals are routine in India's drug-synthesis labs, letting chemists build complex medicines one step at a time.

games.title: Reagent with a carbonyl compound ↔ product
pairs: One equivalent of ROH, dry HCl
Excess ROH with an aldehyde, dry HCl
Ethylene glycol with a ketone, dry HCl

games.title: Addition reactions
items: Addition of HCN is catalysed by a base.
Base generates CN⁻, a stronger nucleophile.
Most ketones readily form stable hydrogensulphite addition compounds.
For most ketones the equilibrium lies to the left for steric reasons.
Dry HCl protonates the carbonyl oxygen in acetal formation.
This makes the carbonyl carbon more electrophilic.
Acetals are hydrolysed back to aldehydes by aqueous mineral acids.
That is why they are used as protecting groups.
Ketones react with Grignard reagents to give primary alcohols.

quiz.q: What is the product when propanone reacts with HCN?
quiz.explain: CN⁻ adds to the carbonyl carbon and OH forms on the same carbon: (CH₃)₂C(OH)CN.
quiz.mistake: Thinks HCN reduces the ketone

quiz.q: Why is the addition of HCN to carbonyl compounds catalysed by a base?
options: The base generates CN⁻, a stronger nucleophile than HCN
The base reduces the carbonyl group
The base protonates the carbonyl oxygen
quiz.explain: HCN is a weak acid; base produces cyanide ions which attack the carbonyl carbon readily.
quiz.mistake: Confuses base and acid catalysis

quiz.q: Why is the NaHSO₃ addition reaction useful?
options: It is used to make cyanohydrins
The crystalline adducts can be separated and then decomposed to recover pure aldehydes
quiz.explain: The reversible adduct formation allows separation and purification.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the reaction is irreversible

quiz.q: What is formed when an aldehyde reacts with one equivalent of a monohydric alcohol in dry HCl?
quiz.explain: One equivalent gives the hemiacetal (alkoxy alcohol); a second equivalent gives the acetal.
quiz.mistake: Skips the hemiacetal stage

quiz.q: What is formed when propanone reacts with ethylene glycol in dry HCl?
quiz.explain: The diol forms a five-membered ring with the carbonyl carbon (ethylene glycol ketal).
quiz.mistake: Confuses ketals with other derivatives

quiz.q: What is the product of the reaction of ethanal with CH₃MgBr followed by hydrolysis?
quiz.explain: An aldehyde other than methanal gives a secondary alcohol: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃.
quiz.mistake: Gives a primary alcohol

quiz.q: Why is dry HCl used in the formation of acetals?
options: It protonates the carbonyl oxygen, increasing the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon
It removes water by reacting with it
quiz.explain: Acid catalysis makes the weakly nucleophilic alcohol able to attack.
quiz.mistake: Thinks HCl supplies a nucleophile

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Ketals are used to protect the carbonyl group of ketones during synthesis. Reason (R): Ketals can be converted back into ketones by hydrolysis with aqueous mineral acid.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: Because the ketal is stable to many reagents but easily hydrolysed when needed, it serves as a protecting group.
quiz.mistake: Does not see why reversibility matters for protection

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can I temporarily protect a ketone during a reaction?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Turn it into a cyclic ketal with ethylene glycol and dry HCl, then get it back by hydrolysis with aqueous acid!
teach.nudge: Which reagent forms the protecting group, and how do you remove it later?

topics.title: Addition of ammonia derivatives and reduction

learn.hook: An orange-red precipitate in the 2,4-DNP test tells a lab technician 'carbonyl group present' within seconds — a favourite of CBSE practical examiners.
points: Ammonia derivatives (H₂N–Z) add to aldehydes and ketones and then lose water, forming >C=N–Z. The reaction is reversible and catalysed by acid.

Products: hydroxylamine (Z = OH) → oxime; hydrazine (Z = NH₂) → hydrazone; phenylhydrazine → phenylhydrazone; 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNP) → 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone (yellow, orange or red solid, used to identify carbonyl compounds); semicarbazide → semicarbazone.
Reduction to alcohols: NaBH₄, LiAlH₄ or catalytic hydrogenation reduce aldehydes to 1° alcohols and ketones to 2° alcohols.

Reduction to hydrocarbons: Clemmensen reduction (zinc amalgam and concentrated HCl) and Wolff–Kishner reduction (hydrazine, then heating with KOH in a high-boiling solvent such as ethylene glycol) convert >C=O into >CH₂.

example.q: How would you convert propanone into propane?
steps: Alternatively, Wolff–Kishner: NH₂NH₂, then KOH/ethylene glycol, heat

learn.reallife: The 2,4-DNP test is used in Class 12 practicals across India to detect aldehydes and ketones in unknown organic samples.

quiz.q: What is formed when an aldehyde reacts with hydroxylamine?
quiz.explain: R–CHO + NH₂OH → R–CH=N–OH + H₂O.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the ammonia derivatives

quiz.q: Which reagent is used to identify aldehydes and ketones by forming coloured precipitates?
quiz.explain: 2,4-DNP derivatives are yellow, orange or red solids.
quiz.mistake: Picks a reagent for alcohols, phenols or amines

quiz.q: What is Clemmensen reduction?
options: Reduction of >C=O to >CH₂ using zinc amalgam and concentrated HCl
Reduction of an acyl chloride to an aldehyde
Reduction of an aldehyde to an alcohol using NaBH₄
quiz.explain: Zn–Hg/HCl removes the oxygen, converting the carbonyl group into a methylene group.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with Wolff–Kishner

quiz.q: Which reduction converts a carbonyl group into CH₂ under basic conditions?
quiz.explain: The hydrazone is heated with KOH in ethylene glycol, giving >CH₂ and N₂.
quiz.mistake: Picks the acidic Clemmensen method

quiz.q: What is obtained when butan-2-one is reduced with NaBH₄?
quiz.explain: NaBH₄ reduces ketones to secondary alcohols.
quiz.mistake: Gives the Clemmensen product

quiz.q: What is the general product of the reaction between a carbonyl compound and H₂N–Z?
quiz.explain: Addition is followed by elimination of water to form a C=N bond.
quiz.mistake: Stops at the addition step

quiz.q: What is the product of ethanal with semicarbazide?
quiz.explain: Semicarbazide (H₂NNHCONH₂) condenses with the aldehyde to form a semicarbazone.
quiz.mistake: Confuses semicarbazide with hydrazine

quiz.q: Assertion (A): The reaction of carbonyl compounds with ammonia derivatives is carried out in weakly acidic medium. Reason (R): Acid protonates the carbonyl oxygen, making the carbon more electrophilic.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.explain: Mild acid activates the carbonyl group (too much acid would protonate the nucleophile).
quiz.mistake: Does not see the role of acid catalysis

teach.ask: Gappu has an unknown liquid: 'How can I quickly show it contains a C=O group?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Add 2,4-DNP: an orange-red precipitate of the hydrazone means a carbonyl group is present!
teach.nudge: Which reagent, and what do you observe?

topics.title: Oxidation, Tollens' and Fehling's tests, and the haloform reaction

learn.hook: A silver mirror on the inside of a test tube is one of the prettiest results in a chemistry lab — and a sure sign of an aldehyde.
points: Aldehydes are easily oxidised to carboxylic acids by HNO₃, KMnO₄, K₂Cr₂O₇ and even mild oxidising agents. Ketones are oxidised only by strong oxidants at high temperature, with C–C bond cleavage, giving acids with fewer carbon atoms.
Tollens' test: warming an aldehyde with freshly prepared ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens' reagent) gives a silver mirror: RCHO + 2[Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ + 3OH⁻ → RCOO⁻ + 2Ag + 2H₂O + 4NH₃.

Fehling's test: Fehling's A (aqueous CuSO₄) and Fehling's B (alkaline sodium potassium tartrate, Rochelle salt) are mixed; aliphatic aldehydes give a reddish-brown precipitate of Cu₂O: RCHO + 2Cu²⁺ + 5OH⁻ → RCOO⁻ + Cu₂O + 3H₂O. Aromatic aldehydes do not give this test.

Haloform reaction: compounds with a CH₃CO– group (methyl ketones and ethanal) are oxidised by sodium hypohalite to the sodium salt of an acid with one carbon less, plus haloform (CHX₃). With NaOI a yellow precipitate of iodoform forms (iodoform test). C=C bonds are not affected.
Distinguishing: Tollens'/Fehling's separate aldehydes from ketones; the iodoform test picks out methyl ketones and ethanal (e.g. pentan-2-one vs pentan-3-one, ethanal vs propanal).

example.q: How would you distinguish between pentan-2-one and pentan-3-one?
steps: Pentan-2-one is CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃, a methyl ketone
Pentan-3-one is CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃, not a methyl ketone
Warm each with I₂ and NaOH: only pentan-2-one gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform
example.answer: Iodoform test: positive for pentan-2-one only

learn.reallife: Mirror makers deposit a silver layer on glass by reducing silver ions with a mild reducing agent such as a sugar — the same chemistry as Tollens' test.

games.title: Oxidation tests
items: Aromatic aldehydes give a positive Fehling's test.
Aromatic aldehydes like benzaldehyde do not respond to Fehling's test.
Ethanal gives a positive iodoform test.
Ketones are oxidised by Tollens' reagent.
Ketones are not oxidised by mild oxidants.
Fehling's test gives a reddish-brown precipitate of Cu₂O.
The haloform reaction gives an acid with one carbon fewer than the methyl ketone.
The CH₃ group leaves as CHX₃.
Strong oxidation of ketones cleaves C–C bonds.
It gives a mixture of acids with fewer carbon atoms.

quiz.q: Which reagent gives a silver mirror with aldehydes?
quiz.explain: Aldehydes reduce [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ to metallic silver, which deposits as a mirror.
quiz.mistake: Confuses Tollens' with Fehling's

quiz.q: What is the reddish-brown precipitate formed in Fehling's test?
quiz.explain: Cu²⁺ is reduced to copper(I) oxide by the aldehyde.
quiz.mistake: Thinks copper metal is deposited

quiz.q: Which compound gives a positive Tollens' test but a negative Fehling's test?
quiz.explain: Aromatic aldehydes reduce Tollens' reagent but do not respond to Fehling's solution.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all aldehydes give both tests

quiz.q: Which compound gives a yellow precipitate with I₂ and NaOH?
quiz.explain: Propanone has the CH₃CO– group needed for the iodoform reaction.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every carbonyl compound gives iodoform

quiz.q: What are the products when CH₃COCH₂CH₃ reacts with NaOI?
quiz.explain: The CH₃ group becomes CHI₃ and the rest becomes the salt of an acid with one carbon fewer (propanoate).
quiz.mistake: Keeps the same number of carbons in the acid

quiz.q: How can ethanal be distinguished from propanal?
options: Iodoform test: only ethanal gives a yellow precipitate
Tollens' test: only propanal gives a silver mirror
Fehling's test: only ethanal gives a precipitate
quiz.explain: Ethanal has the CH₃CO– group; propanal does not. Both give Tollens' and Fehling's tests.
quiz.mistake: Uses a test both compounds pass

quiz.q: Why are ketones not oxidised by Tollens' reagent?
options: They have no H on the carbonyl carbon, and oxidation would need C–C bond cleavage
They are more reactive than aldehydes
quiz.explain: Mild oxidants cannot break C–C bonds, so ketones resist them.
quiz.mistake: Thinks ketones are more easily oxidised

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Benzaldehyde gives a positive Tollens' test. Reason (R): Benzaldehyde gives a positive iodoform test.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
quiz.explain: Benzaldehyde is an aldehyde and reduces Tollens' reagent, but it has no CH₃CO– group, so it gives no iodoform. R is false.
quiz.mistake: Assumes aldehydes give all carbonyl tests

teach.ask: Gappu has propanal and propanone: 'How can I tell them apart in the lab?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Propanal gives a silver mirror with Tollens'; propanone gives a yellow iodoform precipitate. Case solved!
teach.nudge: Which test is positive for the aldehyde, and which for the methyl ketone?

topics.title: α-Hydrogen reactions: aldol and Cannizzaro; ring substitution

learn.hook: Two molecules of ethanal can join hands to make a bigger molecule with a C–C bond — the aldol reaction, one of organic chemistry's most powerful tools.
points: Hydrogens on the carbon next to C=O (α-hydrogens) are acidic because the carbonyl group is strongly electron-withdrawing and the resulting carbanion (enolate) is resonance stabilised.

Aldol reaction: aldehydes/ketones with at least one α-H, in dilute alkali, give β-hydroxy aldehydes (aldols) or β-hydroxy ketones (ketols), which lose water on heating to give α,β-unsaturated compounds. 2CH₃CHO →(dil. NaOH) CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO (3-hydroxybutanal) →(heat, −H₂O) CH₃CH=CHCHO (but-2-enal). 2CH₃COCH₃ →(Ba(OH)₂) 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one → 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one.

Cross aldol condensation between two different compounds that both have α-H gives a mixture of four products. A ketone can be one partner: benzaldehyde + acetophenone (dilute NaOH) gives 1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one (benzalacetophenone).

Cannizzaro reaction: aldehydes without α-H, heated with concentrated alkali, undergo self oxidation–reduction (disproportionation): 2HCHO + conc. KOH → CH₃OH + HCOOK; 2C₆H₅CHO + conc. NaOH → C₆H₅CH₂OH + C₆H₅COONa.
Electrophilic substitution: the –CHO/–COR group is deactivating and meta-directing; benzaldehyde with conc. HNO₃/conc. H₂SO₄ at 273–283 K gives 3-nitrobenzaldehyde.

example.q: Which of these undergo aldol condensation and which undergo Cannizzaro reaction: ethanal, methanal, benzaldehyde, propanone?
example.answer: Aldol: ethanal, propanone; Cannizzaro: methanal, benzaldehyde

learn.reallife: Chalcones (made by cross aldol of benzaldehyde and acetophenone) are being studied in Indian research labs as starting points for anti-inflammatory and anticancer drugs.

games.title: Aldol condensation of ethanal
items: OH⁻ removes an α-hydrogen from ethanal
The enolate ion attacks the carbonyl carbon of a second ethanal

quiz.q: Why are α-hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones acidic?
options: The α-hydrogen is bonded to oxygen
The carbonyl group withdraws electrons and the resulting enolate is resonance stabilised
quiz.explain: Both the electron-withdrawing C=O and delocalisation of the negative charge stabilise the conjugate base.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the hydrogen is on oxygen

quiz.q: What is the product of aldol reaction of ethanal in dilute NaOH (without heating)?
quiz.explain: Two ethanal molecules combine to give the β-hydroxy aldehyde; heating would dehydrate it to but-2-enal.
quiz.mistake: Gives the dehydrated product

quiz.q: What are the products of Cannizzaro reaction of methanal with conc. KOH?
quiz.explain: One HCHO is reduced to CH₃OH and another is oxidised to HCOO⁻K⁺.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only one product forms

quiz.q: Which compound does NOT undergo aldol condensation?
quiz.explain: Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen; it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction instead.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every aldehyde gives aldol

quiz.q: How many products (ignoring stereoisomers) are possible in the cross aldol condensation of ethanal and propanal?
quiz.explain: Two self-condensations and two cross-condensations give four products.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the cross products

quiz.q: What is the product of nitration of benzaldehyde with conc. HNO₃ and conc. H₂SO₄ at 273–283 K?
quiz.explain: The –CHO group is deactivating and meta-directing.
quiz.mistake: Treats –CHO as ortho/para directing

quiz.q: What is formed when benzaldehyde is heated with concentrated NaOH?
quiz.explain: Cannizzaro reaction: one molecule is oxidised to benzoate and another reduced to benzyl alcohol.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it undergoes aldol

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Methanal undergoes Cannizzaro reaction. Reason (R): Methanal has no α-hydrogen atom.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
quiz.explain: Without α-H, enolate formation (aldol) is impossible, so in concentrated alkali it disproportionates.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect α-H with the type of reaction

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Why does ethanal give aldol but benzaldehyde gives Cannizzaro reaction?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Ethanal has α-H to form an enolate (aldol); benzaldehyde has none, so it disproportionates in strong alkali (Cannizzaro)!
teach.nudge: What does ethanal have that benzaldehyde lacks?

topics.title: Uses of carbonyl compounds; naming and structure of carboxylic acids

learn.hook: Red ants sting with formic acid, vinegar gets its tang from acetic acid, and rancid butter smells of butyric acid. Many common names come from these natural sources.
points: Uses of carbonyl compounds: formalin (40% aqueous methanal) preserves biological specimens and is used to make bakelite (phenol–formaldehyde resin) and urea–formaldehyde glues; ethanal is a starting material for acetic acid, ethyl acetate, vinyl acetate, polymers and drugs; benzaldehyde is used in perfumery and dyes; acetone and ethyl methyl ketone are common industrial solvents; vanillin, acetophenone and camphor are prized for odour and flavour.

Carboxylic acids (–COOH): HCOOH formic acid (methanoic acid, from Latin formica, ant); CH₃COOH acetic acid (ethanoic acid, from acetum, vinegar); CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH butyric acid (butanoic acid, from butyrum, butter).

More names: HOOC–COOH oxalic acid (ethanedioic acid); HOOC(CH₂)₄COOH adipic acid (hexanedioic acid); C₆H₅COOH benzoic acid (benzenecarboxylic acid); C₆H₄(COOH)₂ phthalic acid (benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid).

In the carboxyl group, the bonds to the carbon lie in one plane about 120° apart. The carbonyl carbon is less electrophilic than in aldehydes and ketones because the lone pair on the –OH oxygen is delocalised onto the C=O (resonance).

example.q: Give the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂COOH.
steps: Longest chain including COOH: 4 carbons; COOH carbon is C-1

learn.reallife: Formalin is used in Indian medical colleges to preserve specimens, and bakelite from formaldehyde made the classic black electric switches in Indian homes.

quiz.q: What is the IUPAC name of adipic acid?

quiz.q: Which acid gets its name from the Latin word for ant?
quiz.explain: Formica means ant; formic acid was first obtained from red ants.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the origins of the names

quiz.q: Why is the carbonyl carbon of a carboxylic acid less electrophilic than that of an aldehyde?
options: Resonance with the –OH oxygen's lone pair reduces its positive character
quiz.explain: Delocalisation of the lone pair from –OH onto C=O lowers the partial positive charge.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the carboxyl carbon is sp³

quiz.q: What is the IUPAC name of C₆H₅COOH?
quiz.explain: Its common name is benzoic acid; IUPAC calls it benzenecarboxylic acid.
quiz.mistake: Invents a non-standard name

quiz.q: Which compound is used to make bakelite?
quiz.explain: Phenol–formaldehyde resin is bakelite.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with other polymers

quiz.q: What is the IUPAC name of HOOC–COOH?
quiz.explain: Two carbons, each a COOH group.
quiz.mistake: Counts one carbon

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Acetone is widely used as an industrial solvent. Reason (R): Acetone is a ketone that dissolves many organic compounds and is miscible with water.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: Its ability to dissolve a wide range of substances (and mix with water) makes it a useful solvent.
quiz.mistake: Does not link solvent power to its use

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Why is the C=O carbon in an acid less reactive to nucleophiles than in an aldehyde?'
teach.praise: Chirp! The –OH oxygen shares its lone pair with C=O by resonance, so the acid's carbonyl carbon is less positive!
teach.nudge: What does the –OH group do to the carbonyl carbon by resonance?

topics.title: Methods of preparation of carboxylic acids

learn.hook: Need benzoic acid for a food preservative? Start from toluene, from bromobenzene with dry ice, or from benzonitrile. Chemistry offers many roads to the same –COOH.
points: From primary alcohols and aldehydes by oxidation: KMnO₄ (neutral, acidic or alkaline), K₂Cr₂O₇ or CrO₃ in acidic medium (Jones reagent). Aldehydes are oxidised even by mild oxidants.

From alkylbenzenes: vigorous oxidation with chromic acid or acidic/alkaline KMnO₄ converts the entire side chain (primary or secondary alkyl, whatever its length) into –COOH: toluene, ethylbenzene and propylbenzene all give benzoic acid. A tertiary alkyl group is not oxidised.
From nitriles and amides: hydrolysis with H⁺ or OH⁻; nitriles first give amides (under mild conditions the reaction can be stopped there), then acids.
From Grignard reagents: R–MgX + CO₂ (dry ice), then H₃O⁺ → R–COOH, an acid with one more carbon than the alkyl halide.
From acyl halides and anhydrides by hydrolysis with water (with aqueous base they give carboxylate ions); from esters by acidic hydrolysis (acids) or basic hydrolysis (carboxylates, then acidified).

example.q: Convert bromobenzene into benzoic acid.
example.answer: Via the Grignard reagent and CO₂

learn.reallife: Sodium benzoate, the preservative in many Indian sauces and squashes, comes from benzoic acid made industrially by oxidising toluene.

games.title: Nitrile to carboxylic acid
items: Partial hydrolysis gives an amide, R–CONH₂
Further hydrolysis gives the acid (or its salt)
Acidify if alkali was used, to obtain R–COOH

quiz.q: What is obtained when propylbenzene is oxidised vigorously with alkaline KMnO₄ followed by acidification?
quiz.explain: The entire side chain is oxidised to –COOH regardless of its length.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the chain stays intact

quiz.q: What is formed when CH₃CH₂MgBr reacts with dry ice followed by acid hydrolysis?
quiz.explain: CO₂ adds one carbon: C₂H₅–COOH.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the carbon added from CO₂

quiz.q: How many carbon atoms are in the acid formed from 1-bromobutane via its Grignard reagent and CO₂?
quiz.explain: Butyl (4 C) + 1 C from CO₂ = pentanoic acid.
quiz.mistake: Does not count the carbon from CO₂

quiz.q: Which intermediate forms during the hydrolysis of a nitrile to a carboxylic acid?
quiz.explain: R–CN → R–CONH₂ → R–COOH.
quiz.mistake: Confuses hydrolysis with reduction

quiz.q: Which reagent is known as Jones reagent for oxidising primary alcohols to acids?
quiz.explain: Chromium trioxide in acidic medium oxidises 1° alcohols to carboxylic acids.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with PCC, which stops at the aldehyde

quiz.q: What are the products of alkaline hydrolysis of ethyl ethanoate?
quiz.explain: Basic hydrolysis (saponification) gives the carboxylate salt and the alcohol.
quiz.mistake: Gives the acidic hydrolysis products

quiz.q: Which alkylbenzene is NOT oxidised to benzoic acid by hot KMnO₄?
quiz.explain: Oxidation needs a benzylic hydrogen; the tertiary carbon in tert-butylbenzene has none.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every side chain is oxidised

quiz.q: Assertion (A): Toluene and ethylbenzene both give benzoic acid on vigorous oxidation. Reason (R): The entire side chain of an alkylbenzene (primary or secondary) is oxidised to –COOH regardless of its length.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.explain: Whatever the length of the side chain, only the carbon attached to the ring remains, as –COOH.
quiz.mistake: Expects longer chains to give longer acids

teach.ask: Gappu has CH₃Br: 'How can I make an acid with one more carbon atom from it?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Make the Grignard reagent, add dry ice (CO₂), then acidify: CH₃Br becomes CH₃COOH!
teach.nudge: Which reagent adds the extra carbon, and what do you do at the end?

topics.title: Physical properties and acidity of carboxylic acids

learn.hook: Acetic acid boils at 391 K, way above ethanol, even though their masses are similar. And it fizzes with baking soda, which phenol cannot do.
points: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than aldehydes, ketones and even alcohols of similar mass, because of extensive hydrogen bonding. Many exist as hydrogen-bonded dimers in the vapour phase and in aprotic solvents.

Simple aliphatic acids up to four carbons are miscible with water (H-bonding); solubility falls as the chain grows. Benzoic acid is nearly insoluble in cold water. Acids also dissolve in less polar solvents like benzene, ether and chloroform.

Acids react with metals (giving H₂), with alkalis (salt + water), and with weak bases such as NaHCO₃, giving brisk effervescence of CO₂ — a test that phenols do not pass: R–COOH + NaHCO₃ → R–COONa + H₂O + CO₂.

Acid strength: Ka = [H₃O⁺][RCOO⁻]/[RCOOH], pKa = −log Ka; smaller pKa means a stronger acid. Carboxylic acids (pKa about 4–5, e.g. CH₃COOH 4.76, C₆H₅COOH 4.19, HCOOH 3.75) are weaker than mineral acids but stronger than phenols (≈10) and alcohols (≈16), because the carboxylate ion has two equivalent resonance structures with the negative charge on two electronegative oxygen atoms.

Electron-withdrawing groups increase acidity (CCl₃COOH > CHCl₂COOH > CH₂ClCOOH > CH₃COOH; FCH₂COOH > ClCH₂COOH > BrCH₂COOH), with a smaller effect the farther they are from –COOH. Electron-donating groups (alkyl) decrease acidity; a phenyl or vinyl group directly attached increases it relative to acetic acid.

example.q: An acid has Ka = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵. What is its pKa, and is it stronger or weaker than acetic acid (pKa 4.76)?
steps: A larger pKa means a weaker acid
example.answer: pKa = 5; it is slightly weaker than acetic acid

learn.reallife: Vinegar used in Indian kitchens for pickles and chutneys is about 5% acetic acid; a pinch of baking soda makes it fizz with CO₂ — the classic acid test.

games.title: Acidity facts
items: Carboxylic acids liberate CO₂ from NaHCO₃.
They are strong enough acids to react with bicarbonate.
Phenol is too weak an acid.
A lower pKa means a stronger acid.
Fluoroacetic acid is weaker than acetic acid.
F withdraws electrons and makes it much stronger.
The inductive effect weakens with distance.
